wayland-protocols-misc@0.3.12.protocol_origin: A copy of KDE's server-decoration.xml, kept in the wayland-rs repository. The LGPL text comes from https://github.com/KDE/plasma-wayland-protocols/tree/3d8327f5c8727702c5b14730c32d70b30e2ae106.
wayland-protocols-misc@0.3.12.used_by: smithay-client-toolkit 0.20.0, through smithay-clipboard, uses only the input-method protocol from this crate.
wayland-protocols-misc@0.3.12.license_text_note: The crate ships only its MIT LICENSE.txt, so licenses/rust/manifest.json supplies the LGPL text from the KDE commit above.

wayland-protocols-plasma@0.3.12.used_by: winit 0.30.13 always enables this crate with its wayland feature, for KDE blur only. ReShiki never requests blur.

facts: Both crates declare MIT, but wayland-scanner generates their Rust code at build time from the KDE protocol descriptions listed under files, which are LGPL-2.1-or-later. The other bundled descriptions are MIT-CMU, MIT or BSD-3-Clause, or carry no license header (fullscreen-shell.xml). xml_inventory_sha256 pins every bundled XML file: the SHA-256 of the sorted lines "<path> <sha256>\n". Both crates are Linux-only dependencies of ReShiki.
binary_content: wayland-scanner 0.31.11's client generator emits protocol metadata from the descriptions: interface, request, event and argument names, message signatures, versions and flags. Description text becomes doc comments, which compilation drops. On 2026-11-25, `strings -n 6 reshiki | grep '^org_kde_'` on a Linux aarch64 release build with these crate versions found org_kde_* interface names, and searches for SPDX-FileCopyrightText, SPDX-License-Identifier: LGPL and a plasma-shell.xml description sentence found nothing. That build was not kept.
reason: The project owner chose to keep these crates and treat their KDE files as LGPL-2.1-or-later in the notices. Only protocol metadata generated from the descriptions reaches the binary. By analogy with LGPL-2.1 section 5, object code that uses only numerical parameters, data structure layouts and accessors, and small macros and inline functions (ten lines or less) from a library's header material may be used without restriction, although section 6 still governs an executable that also contains portions of the library itself. The notices ship the complete LGPL-2.1 text and each file's copyright block with this record. ReShiki's complete source, Cargo.lock and build instructions are public, so a recipient can modify these crates and rebuild. ReShiki does not relicense the protocol descriptions.
review: This record covers only the package versions, sources, checksums and file digests above. license_notices.py fails when either crate has an unreviewed version, source, license declaration, XML inventory or license text. check_agent_dependencies.py fails when Cargo.lock holds either crate without a reviewed version, source and checksum.
